messages:
morgan: Heads-up — noticed duplicate IO during sideloaded delta warmups. Coordinator A claims, starts streaming, then TTL lapses and Coordinator B reclaims same shards. Result: extra mmap churn and occasional OOM spikes.

sophia: Reproduced on canary. Crash+restart increases the chance. We need a light ownership primitive for warmup rather than pure TTL-based heuristics.

raj: Agree on lease token. Need to define who decides eviction: the warmup coordinator or the global evictor?

elise: Concern: locks or sync points can slow hotstart. Can we make renewals best-effort async so hotstarts don't block?

morgan: Draft API sketch:
```
claim(shard_ids, expected_manifest_hash?) -> { token: "tok123", expiry: 167... }
pin(token, shard_ids) -> ok|conflict
release(token)
```
Coordinator does cheap claim, streams data, then does a pin (strong) before advertising availability. Evictor checks token expiry and optional liveness table before evicting.

sophia: Strong +1 for including manifest hash in claim to avoid hotstarting from mutated bundles. If manifest mismatch, claim fails fast.

raj: Failure modes: process crash while holding token -> stale tokens. Token should include owner id+epoch. Evictor should perform heartbeat/liveness check and treat tokens with missing heartbeats as reclaimable after TTL. Tombstone marker on release helps debugging.

elise: Hot-path optimization: make claim immediate and non-blocking. Coordinator streams and only blocks briefly on pin (single metadata write). If pin loses, abort and let another coordinator pick up.

morgan: Exactly. Claim is reservation; pin is the commit. Partial state cleaned up on abort.

sophia: Implementation detail: add manifest-sidecar field `sideload.allow_hot_start` default false so older exporters remain conservative.

raj: Telemetry: emit events for claim/pin/renew/release and track duplicate-read counter for cold starts.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out prefetch-coordinator-v2 to staging (30% canary). Token endpoints: POST /v2/weights/claim, POST /v2/weights/pin.

morgan: Action items:
- morgan: open RFC PR describing API + failure modes
- sophia: prototype manifest-hash check + exporter sidecar change
- raj: add token liveness checks + telemetry to evictor
- elise: run load tests for async renewals and measure latency impact

sophia: Will branch prototype today and attach to RFC. Keeping pin as a single fast write is ideal. :thumbsup: 

morgan: I'll add sequence diagram to RFC and iterate after staging telemetry.

elise: One more thought: consider a "sideload-only" namespace for tiny delta shards so eviction heuristics treat them differently from large base shards. Could reduce contention.

raj: Sounds like a follow-up if staging shows contention. For now keep token API generic.

morgan: PR WIP: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/869

infra-bot: canary-health: staging cohort healthy.
